Clinical actions were assessed only in internally managed patients with valid (non-QNS, non-cancelled) results, as complete clinical documentation was available exclusively for this subgroup. The two rows under Overall Management Change Status are mutually exclusive and together sum to the total assessed (N). Specific clinical actions are not mutually exclusive: individual patients may have had more than one action documented, so subcategory counts may not sum to the parent total. Additional diagnostic workup is independent of management change status; patients in this row may also appear in either the documented-change or no-documented-change group above. Responses of "Y" and "VAN" were both counted as positive for additional testing. Blank entries were excluded from denominators. The targeted therapies listed are illustrative examples; actual agents were confirmed by chart review.

Pre-analytical Correlation Analyses

Supplementary analyses examining whether specimen-level pre-analytical factors (fluid volume, QNS classification) are associated with assay output.

Note on the unit of analysis: fluid volume is a property of the physical aspiration, not the assay run. When a single specimen is tested across multiple assays (e.g., PIK3CA + TEK + BRAF), the same fluid volume appears on each row. Volume-based analyses therefore deduplicate to one row per aspiration (unique patient × volume combination) to avoid double-counting; this is referred to as “aspiration-level” below. The Spearman analysis is the only exception — it remains test-level because wild-type droplet counts are measured per assay run.

Spearman correlations: fluid volume vs. wild-type droplet counts

Spearman rank correlation (non-parametric, distribution-free). Test-level analysis: one entry per assay run (not aspiration-level), because wild-type droplet counts are measured separately for each assay. n therefore differs from aspiration-level QNS analyses where appropriate (Table 2, Supplemental Tables). Restricted to PIK3CA Multiplex valid tests with measured fluid volume > 0. Correlations not reported where n < 4.

Aspiration-level analysis: one entry per unique patient × volume combination, restricted to specimens with measured fluid volume > 0. Excludes 22 of 135 valid tests and 2 of 19 QNS tests with missing or zero fluid volume. Two-sided Mann–Whitney U test (Wilcoxon rank-sum). A lower median volume in the QNS group would suggest that low-volume specimens are at higher risk of failing the assay.
